description:
Every command arm that accepts the machine-readable output flag reports failures reached after successful argument parsing and command dispatch in the structured error envelope, so a machine consumer never has to parse a plain-text command diagnostic.

## Background

The machine-readable contract covered success output but not post-dispatch failure. An arm that rendered the envelope on failure did so by classifying the error at its own call site through several distinct mechanisms, including a shared macro, named helpers, and inline sites that printed an envelope and exited directly. An arm that instead propagated its error with a bare `?` reached the top-level printer, which wrote a plain-text `Error: <message>` line to stderr and left stdout empty. The plain-text form carried no error code, no structured detail, and nothing a JSON parser could read.

The command definitions and generated conformance census are the authority for the live arm set; the current census is emitted under the active Cargo profile at `jit-conformance/failure-probe-census.json`. The planning baseline showed that roughly half of the flag-accepting arms had no envelope route on a post-dispatch failure path, while several others classified only one error class and propagated the rest. Invocation against missing or invalid command inputs confirmed that the defect crossed namespaces rather than being universal or confined to one command family.

Exit codes diverged as well. Multiple arms exited differently under the flag than without it because the code string their envelope carried was absent from the registered error-code vocabulary and fell through to the generic class. The generated exit-code reference documented the plain-path values, and its binding test exercised only the plain path, so the projection was accurate for one invocation form and silently wrong for the other.

The `doc` namespace is where the defect surfaced: its command arms propagated post-dispatch failures with bare `?`, while `doc dir` had already established the repair pattern of classifying the failure by downcast and handing the envelope to the shared macro.

This surface is what the MCP bridge is generated from. An agent consumer reaching an unstructured post-dispatch failure received `EXECUTION_ERROR` with the plain-text diagnostic embedded in a shell-command string, so the failure reason was undecodable without parsing prose.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A census derived from the command definitions, rather than from sampling, records for every arm accepting the machine-readable output flag whether its post-dispatch failure path renders the structured envelope.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every arm accepting the flag renders failures reached after successful argument parsing and command dispatch as the structured error envelope carrying a classified error code, with no such failure reaching the top-level plain-text printer.
- [hard] REQ-03: A post-dispatch failing invocation under the flag emits no plain-text diagnostic on the stream that carries the envelope.
- [hard] REQ-04: A converted arm's process exit code equals the code its envelope reports, and post-dispatch failures of the same class exit identically across arms.
- [hard] REQ-05: Regression coverage drives a post-dispatch failing invocation of every converted arm and asserts envelope structure and error classification rather than a copied message string.
- [hard] REQ-06: A repository check fails when an arm accepting the flag can reach the top-level plain-text printer on a post-dispatch failure, so a newly added arm cannot ship without the envelope.
- [hard] REQ-07: Adopter documentation states the post-dispatch machine-readable failure contract — envelope shape, error code, exit code — once, in a single canonical home.

## Non-goals

- Changing Clap argument-parser diagnostics, help output, or version exits before command dispatch.
- Changing the human-readable failure output of a dispatched command.
- Restructuring the success-side envelope or its collection wrapper.
- Renaming or removing any error code a command already emits.
- Adding the flag to command arms that do not accept it today.

## Notes

- Scope is the whole post-dispatch command surface rather than the `doc` namespace alone, and delivery is in milestone v1.0: the plain-text post-dispatch failure form is a release-visible contract defect on the surface generated agent tooling consumes, and a repair pattern was already established in the tree.
- REQ-04 requires the exit code to follow the reported code. The code strings themselves stay, which is why the non-goal above forbids renaming rather than forbidding all vocabulary change.
- REQ-07 is subject to `@/charter/D-13`: one canonical home per adopter-facing fact.
- REQ-06 is what separates this from a sweep. A census goes stale when a new arm is added, so the guard is the durable half of the work.
title: Structured failure reporting across the machine-readable CLI surface
